description: A JSON-RPC notification is forwarded like any other POST: the SDK does not parse JSON-RPC, does not answer 202 itself and does not inject, strip or generate Mcp-Session-Id. 202 for notifications is the MCP handler's job, so with an echo handler the response is the handler's 200. MCPWARP.md §4 (I1)
in:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: notes-tester.mcpwarp.test
accept: application/json, text/event-stream
content-type: application/json
mcp-session-id: abc
user-agent: Go-http-client/1.1
Content-Length: 54

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}
out:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

36
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}
0
notes: The same pass-through holds for GET without an SSE Accept (405 + Allow: POST is the handler's answer) and DELETE. Chunk boundaries are not normative.
